strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Masquerading via File Type Modification

analytics.name: Analytic 0630
analytics.guidance: Detects behavior where files with non-executable or misleading extensions (e.g., .jpg, .txt) are created or modified but subsequently executed as binaries based on internal file headers or abnormal parent process lineage. This includes identifying polyglot files or malformed magic bytes indicative of masquerading attempts.

tuning.description: List of non-executable file types commonly used to mask payloads (.jpg, .txt, .gif)
Targeted directories for initial access and downloads (e.g., %TEMP%, Downloads, AppData)
Detection tolerance for mismatches between extension and file signature (magic bytes)
Time range between file creation and first execution
Anomaly score threshold for suspicious parent-child process combinations

analytics.name: Analytic 0631
analytics.guidance: Detects when a script or binary is named with misleading or benign-looking extensions (.jpg, .doc) and is then executed via command line or a scheduled task. Includes ELF header mismatches and content-type inconsistencies on disk.

tuning.description: Whether to parse file signatures or MIME types from file headers
Monitored directory scope for adversarial execution (e.g., /tmp/, /home/username/Downloads)

log_sources.name: linux:osquery
log_sources.channel: Read headers and detect MIME type mismatch

analytics.name: Analytic 0632
analytics.guidance: Detects binaries disguised as media or document types through extension-only masquerading or by modifying the file signature. Observes execution of files whose extension is not typically executable (.jpg, .txt), yet have valid Mach-O headers or execute via Terminal or launch services.

tuning.description: Scope of services monitored for unusual launches (e.g., Finder, Terminal, Preview)
How strictly the detection checks header validity vs. file extension
Time range for linking file modification and execution events
